I couldn't do this research. My first attempt to fetch the source pages (Enduring Word on Ezekiel 23, the Bible Hub commentaries on vv. 4, 14 and 23, and Gill on StudyLight) was blocked, and the tool said I have no lookups left for this turn. I didn't read any pages, so I have nothing sourced to give you.

I could write notes from what I already know about Ezekiel 23, but your rules say to report only what the pages say and give a URL for every point. Anything I wrote now wouldn't meet that, so I've left it out.

If you send the request again in a new turn, I'll start with these sources:

1. **Traditional reading:** Enduring Word on Ezekiel 23, the commentaries on Bible Hub for each verse (Ellicott, Pulpit, Gill, Barnes, Keil and Delitzsch), and Precept Austin.
2. **Differences between Protestant traditions:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon (spurgeon.org), Ligonier and The Gospel Coalition, and Lutheran material on lcms.org and 1517.org.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes (on the names Oholah and Oholibah, and on Pekod, Shoa and Koa in v. 23), Bible Odyssey (on the marriage metaphor and debates about its sexual violence), and Catholic and Orthodox sources such as newadvent.org.

It may help to split the passage into two requests, vv. 1–10 and vv. 11–24, so each one stays within the lookup limit.
